Kill Yusuf or cast him out to some land, so that your father's face will be yours alone, and after that you can be righteous people" (12:8-9). One of them said: "Do not kill Yusuf, but throw him into the bottom of the well; some travellers will pick him up" (12:10). A Muslim learns how envy talks itself into wrong by promising repentance later.

question: What did Yusuf's brothers bring their father to make him believe a wolf had eaten him?
answers: His shirt stained with false blood
explanation: "They brought his shirt with false blood on it"; Ya'qub replied: "Patience is most fitting."
detail: The brothers came to their father at night weeping, saying a wolf had eaten Yusuf while they raced (12:16-17). "They brought his shirt with false blood on it. He said: Rather, your souls have tempted you to something; so patience is most fitting, and Allah is the one whose help is sought" (12:18). The shirt returns twice: torn from behind, proving Yusuf innocent (12:26-28), and laid over Ya'qub's face, restoring his sight (12:93, 12:96). A Muslim learns from Ya'qub to meet a lie with patience and seek Allah's help.

question: What did Allah promise Musa's mother when inspiring her to place him in the river?
answers: To return him to her and make him a messenger
explanation: "Do not fear and do not grieve: We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers."
detail: "We inspired the mother of Musa: when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve; We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers" (28:7). Pharaoh's family picked him up (28:8). Allah made him refuse every wet nurse until his sister led them to his mother, "so that she might know that the promise of Allah is true" (28:12-13). A Muslim learns that Allah's promise is kept, even through a river and a palace.

question: With what did Musa strike the sea so that it parted?
explanation: "Strike the sea with your staff": it parted, and each side was like a great mountain.
detail: The verse reads: "We inspired Musa: Strike the sea with your staff. So it parted, and each part was like a great mountain" (26:63). Just before, when the two hosts saw each other, Musa's companions cried that they would be overtaken, and he answered: "No; my Lord is with me, He will guide me" (26:62). Allah then saved Musa and all who were with him and drowned the others (26:65-66). A Muslim learns that Musa's certainty came before the sea opened, not after.

question: What was the first thing Allah told Musa when addressing him?
answers: "I am Allah, there is no god but Me: worship Me and establish prayer"
explanation: "Indeed, I am Allah; there is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance."
detail: Musa had gone towards a fire and heard a call: take off your sandals, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa, listen to what is revealed (20:11-13). What was revealed came at once: "Indeed, I am Allah; there is no god but Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance" (20:14). The next verse tells him that the Hour is surely coming (20:15). A Muslim learns that Allah's first message to a prophet was His oneness, worship and prayer.

question: How did Allah tell Musa and Harun to speak to Pharaoh?
explanation: "Go to Pharaoh… and speak to him with gentle speech; perhaps he may be reminded or fear."
detail: The command reads: "Go, both of you, to Pharaoh; he has transgressed. Speak to him with gentle speech, so that he may be reminded or fear" (20:43-44). The two said they feared Pharaoh would hasten harm against them, and Allah answered: "Do not fear; I am with you both, I hear and I see" (20:45-46). Gentleness was commanded towards the man the Qur'an calls a transgressor. A Muslim learns that a firm message is to be delivered in a gentle voice.

question: What did Musa tell his young servant at the start of his journey to the junction of the two seas?
answers: That he would not stop until he reached the junction of the two seas
That he wanted to go home
That he was looking for gold
explanation: "I will not give up until I reach the junction of the two seas, even if I go on for ages."
detail: The verse reads: "When Musa said to his young servant: I will not give up until I reach the junction of the two seas, even if I go on for ages" (18:60). When they reached it they forgot their fish (18:61); when Musa later asked for their meal, the boy remembered it, and Musa said: "That is what we were seeking", and they turned back (18:62-64). There they found a servant given mercy and knowledge from Allah (18:65). A Muslim learns that seeking knowledge is worth a long, tiring journey.

question: Which of these did the knowledgeable servant do in front of Musa, who did not understand at the time?
answers: He made a hole in a boat
explanation: He holed the boat, then killed a boy, then straightened a wall — and afterwards explained each act to Musa.
detail: The servant holed the ship they boarded, and Musa asked: "Have you holed it to drown its people?" (18:71). Then he killed a boy (18:74). Then he repaired a falling wall, and Musa said he could have taken payment (18:77). The servant explained each act: a king was seizing every sound boat, the boy's parents were believers, and the wall hid a treasure for two orphans; "I did not do it of my own accord" (18:82). A Muslim learns that what looks like harm can hide Allah's mercy.

question: What were Isa's first words, still in the cradle?
answers: "I am the servant of Allah; He gave me the Scripture and made me a prophet"
explanation: "He said: indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet."
detail: Maryam brought the child to her people, who reproached her (19:27-28). She pointed to the baby, and they asked how they could speak to a child in the cradle (19:29). "He said: I am the servant of Allah; He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet" (19:30). He went on: Allah had made him blessed wherever he was, enjoined on him prayer and zakat, and made him dutiful to his mother (19:31-32). A Muslim learns that Isa's first word about himself was "servant".

question: What did Adam and his wife say to Allah after eating from the tree?
answers: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; if You do not forgive us, we will be lost"
explanation: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."
detail: Allah had forbidden Adam and his wife one tree, and Satan whispered to them (7:19-21). When they tasted it, their nakedness appeared, and their Lord asked: "Did I not forbid you that tree and tell you that Satan is a clear enemy to you?" (7:22). They answered: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers" (7:23). A Muslim learns the words to say after a mistake.

question: What mission did Allah give Nuh towards his people, in the first verse of Surah Nuh?
answers: To warn them before a painful punishment came to them
explanation: "We sent Nuh to his people: warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment."
detail: The surah opens: "We sent Nuh to his people: Warn your people before a painful punishment comes to them" (71:1). Nuh told them he was a clear warner and called them to worship Allah, fear Him and obey him (71:2-3). He told his Lord that he had called them night and day and they only fled, putting their fingers in their ears (71:5-7). He promised them rain, wealth and children if they sought forgiveness (71:10-12). A Muslim learns that a warning is an act of mercy, given before punishment.

question: What were Adam and his wife forbidden to approach in the Garden?
explanation: Allah allowed them to eat freely, except to approach one single tree.
detail: The command is given in Surah Al-Baqarah: "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat freely from it wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers" (2:35). It comes right after the angels prostrated to Adam and Iblis refused (2:34), and right before Satan made the two of them slip (2:36). A Muslim learns that obedience is proved at the single limit Allah sets, not in the abundance He permits.

question: According to the Quran, what did Adam receive from his Lord after his lapse?
answers: Words (of repentance), and Allah accepted his repentance
explanation: "Then Adam received words from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance."
detail: The verse reads: "Then Adam received words from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance. He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful" (2:37). Surah Al-A'raf records the prayer of Adam and his wife: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will be among the losers" (7:23). A Muslim learns that the way back to Allah was opened for the first human being.

question: Whom does the Quran compare 'Isa to, as regards his creation?
explanation: "Indeed, the likeness of 'Isa before Allah is as the likeness of Adam: He created him from dust, then said to him 'Be' and he was."
detail: The verse reads: "The likeness of 'Isa before Allah is as the likeness of Adam: He created him from dust, then said to him 'Be', and he was" (3:59). Surah Al-'Imran has just told of the birth of 'Isa, and the next verse closes the argument: "The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters" (3:60). A Muslim takes from it that 'Isa is a created servant and messenger, and that a wonder in birth points to the Creator.

question: Of which prophet does the Quran say he was truthful and that Allah raised him to a high station?
explanation: "And mention Idris in the Book: he was truthful, a prophet; and We raised him to a high station."
detail: Surah Maryam says: "Mention in the Book Idris. He was a man of truth, a prophet. And We raised him to a high station" (19:56-57). He closes a series of prophets the surah tells the Prophet ﷺ to mention: Ibrahim (19:41), Musa (19:51), Isma'il (19:54), then Idris. The surah then gathers them all as those on whom Allah bestowed favour, who fell in prostration and weeping when His verses were recited (19:58). A Muslim learns that Idris is honoured for two things named together, truthfulness and prophethood.

question: What did Nuh say as his people boarded the ark?
answers: "In the name of Allah be its sailing and its anchorage"
explanation: "Board it: in the name of Allah be its course and its mooring."
detail: Nuh's words are in Surah Hud: "Board it: in the name of Allah shall be its course and its anchorage. My Lord is Forgiving and Merciful" (11:41). The verse before has the oven gushing forth as the sign that the flood had begun, with the order to load a pair of every kind and the few who believed (11:40). A Muslim learns from Nuh to begin any journey with the name of Allah, trusting Him for the setting out and the arrival.

question: In Surah Nuh, what did the prophet Nuh ask his Lord concerning the disbelievers?
answers: To leave none of them on the earth
To give them one more year
explanation: "My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant."
detail: The prayer closes Surah Nuh: "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any inhabitant from among the disbelievers. If You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and beget none but wicked disbelievers" (71:26-27). It comes after Nuh tells his Lord that he called his people night and day, and that his call only increased them in flight (71:5-6); the Qur'an counts his stay among them as a thousand years less fifty (29:14). A Muslim learns that Nuh asked this only after a lifetime of patient calling.

question: How many of each kind was Nuh to take aboard the ark?
explanation: Allah commanded him to load into it a pair of each kind, along with his family.
detail: The order is in Surah Al-Mu'minun: "Construct the ship under Our eyes and Our inspiration, and when Our command comes and the oven overflows, take into it a pair of every kind, and your family, except those against whom the word has gone forth" (23:27). Just before, his people had called him only a man like themselves, and he prayed: "My Lord, help me, because they have denied me" (23:26). A Muslim learns that Allah's rescue came with exact instructions, and Nuh answered it with praise (23:28).

question: Hud reminded 'Ad that Allah had made them successors after which people?
explanation: "Remember when He made you successors after the people of Nuh and increased you in stature extensively."
detail: Hud says to 'Ad in Surah Al-A'raf: "Remember when He made you successors after the people of Nuh and increased you amply in stature. So remember the favours of Allah, that you may succeed" (7:69). He had begun like every prophet, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him" (7:65), and the chiefs answered that they saw him in foolishness (7:66). A Muslim learns that a people's strength is a favour to be remembered, and that remembering it is the road to success.

question: By what were the people of 'Ad destroyed, according to Surah Al-Haqqah?
explanation: "As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a screaming, violent wind."
detail: Surah Al-Haqqah says: "As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a screaming, violent wind, which He imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people there lying fallen, as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees" (69:6-7). The surah pairs them with Thamud, who "were destroyed by the overpowering blast" (69:5). A Muslim learns that the wind that serves us daily is a soldier of Allah, and that no strength stands against Him.

question: What did Hud reproach his people for, who built on every high place?
answers: Building out of vanity and hoping to live forever
explanation: "Do you build on every elevation a sign, amusing yourselves, and take for yourselves palaces as if you would live forever?"
detail: Hud asks in Surah Ash-Shu'ara: "Do you build on every high place a monument, amusing yourselves, and take for yourselves fortresses, as if you would live forever?" (26:128-129). He had opened with the call the surah gives every messenger, "Will you not fear Allah?" (26:124), and he goes on to name the One who provided them with cattle, children, gardens and springs (26:132-134). A Muslim learns to use wealth for need and gratitude rather than show, remembering that the earth is not a permanent home.

question: What did Thamud do with the mountains, according to the Quran?
answers: They carved houses out of them
explanation: "You take for yourselves palaces from its plains and carve from the mountains, homes."
detail: Salih says to Thamud in Surah Al-A'raf: "Remember when He made you successors after 'Ad and settled you in the land: you take palaces from its plains and carve homes out of the mountains. So remember the favours of Allah, and do not go about the earth spreading corruption" (7:74). Just before, he had shown them the she-camel of Allah as a sign, telling them not to touch her with harm (7:73). A Muslim learns that a people's craft comes from Allah, and the right answer is gratitude.

question: According to Surah Al-Qamar, the she-camel was sent to Thamud as what?
explanation: "Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them, so watch them and be patient."
detail: Allah tells Salih in Surah Al-Qamar: "We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them, so watch them and be patient. And inform them that the water is to be shared between them: each drinking turn is to be attended" (54:27-28). Thamud had refused to follow "one human being from among us" and called Salih an insolent liar (54:24-25). They failed the trial: their companion hamstrung her (54:29). A Muslim learns that a sign from Allah is also a test of how one treats it.

question: What seized Thamud after they killed the she-camel?
explanation: "So the earthquake seized them, and they lay fallen in their homes."
detail: Surah Al-A'raf tells the end: "So the earthquake seized them, and morning found them lying prone in their homes" (7:78). The verse before gives the cause: they hamstrung the she-camel, scorned the command of their Lord and dared Salih, "Bring us what you promise us, if you are one of the messengers" (7:77). A Muslim learns that a punishment demanded in mockery can come, and that the prophet's advice was the true protection.

question: Which prophet was sent to the people who committed the great indecency, saying "Will you not fear Allah?"
explanation: "When their brother Lut said to them: 'Will you not fear Allah?'"
detail: Surah Ash-Shu'ara records: "When their brother Lut said to them: Will you not fear Allah? I am a trustworthy messenger to you, so fear Allah and obey me. I ask you no reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds" (26:161-164). The surah gives the same opening words to Nuh, Hud and Salih, each introduced as "their brother" too. A Muslim learns that Lut came to his people as a brother, with the call every messenger brought.

question: What was Lut commanded to do on the night of the punishment?
answers: Set out by night with his family and not look back
explanation: "So set out with your family during a portion of the night, and let none of you look back."
detail: The angels tell Lut in Surah Hud: "We are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. So set out with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you look back, except your wife: she will be struck by what strikes them. Their appointed time is the morning" (11:81). At dawn the city was turned upside down and rained with stones of baked clay (11:82). A Muslim learns that obeying Allah's instructions without looking back was the way out.

question: Which prophet was sent to the people of Madyan, who cheated in measure and weight?
explanation: Shu'ayb ordered them to give full measure and just weight, and not to spread corruption in the land.
detail: Surah Hud says: "And to Madyan, their brother Shu'ayb. He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. And do not give short measure and weight. I see you in prosperity, and I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day" (11:84). He goes on: "Give full measure and weight in justice, and do not deprive people of their due" (11:85). Worship of Allah alone and honest scales stand in one breath. A Muslim learns that fair dealing in trade is part of faith.

question: What did Shu'ayb tell his people he really wanted?
answers: "I only intend reform, as much as I am able"
explanation: "I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allah."
detail: Shu'ayb says in Surah Hud: "I do not want to do, in your absence, what I forbid you. I only intend reform, as much as I am able. My success is only through Allah; in Him I trust, and to Him I turn" (11:88). His people had just mocked him: "Does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worshipped?" (11:87). A Muslim learns that whoever calls to good must live by it first, and count on Allah for the result.

question: After Allah tested Ibrahim with commands that he fulfilled, what did He say to him?
answers: "I will make you a leader (imam) for the people"
"I will make you king of Babylon"
explanation: "I will make you a leader for the people." Ibrahim asked: "And of my descendants?"
detail: Surah Al-Baqarah says: "When Ibrahim was tried by his Lord with words and he fulfilled them, He said: I will make you a leader for the people. He said: And of my descendants? He said: My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers" (2:124). The verses after show what that leadership meant: the House made a place of return and safety, and Ibrahim and Isma'il raising its foundations, praying "Our Lord, accept from us" (2:125-127). A Muslim learns that leadership in religion is given for obedience fulfilled, not inherited by blood.

question: How did Ibrahim silence the king who claimed to give life and death?
answers: "Allah brings the sun from the east; bring it from the west"
explanation: "Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west." The disbeliever was overwhelmed.
detail: Surah Al-Baqarah tells it: "When Ibrahim said: My Lord is the One who gives life and causes death, he said: I give life and cause death. Ibrahim said: Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west. So the one who disbelieved was confounded" (2:258). The verse says the man argued "because Allah had given him kingship" and leaves him unnamed. A Muslim learns to answer a false claim with a clear proof no power on earth can imitate.

question: What was Ibrahim commanded to proclaim to the people about the Sacred House?
answers: The pilgrimage: they will come on foot and on every lean camel
explanation: "And proclaim to the people the Hajj: they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel."
detail: The command reads: "Proclaim the pilgrimage to the people: they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every distant pass" (22:27). The verse before sets the scene: Allah settled Ibrahim at the site of the House with the order to associate nothing with Him and to purify it for those who circle it, stand, bow and prostrate (22:26). A Muslim learns that the Hajj is an invitation first issued by Ibrahim, and every pilgrim today answers it.

question: What did Ibrahim serve his honoured guests, which they did not touch?
explanation: He went to his household and brought a fat calf; seeing their hands not reaching for it, he felt fear.
detail: Surah Adh-Dhariyat tells it: "When they entered upon him and said: Peace. He said: Peace, unfamiliar people. Then he slipped away to his family and brought a fat calf, and placed it before them and said: Will you not eat?" (51:24-27). When their hands did not reach for it he grew afraid; they said, "Do not fear", and gave him the good news of a boy of knowledge (51:28). A Muslim learns hospitality from Ibrahim: return the greeting, go quietly, bring the best, set it close, and invite gently.

question: Of whom does the Quran say he is "an excellent example" (uswa hasana) for the believers, along with those with him?
explanation: "There has been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim and those with him."
detail: Surah Al-Mumtahanah says: "There has been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim and those with him, when they said to their people: We are clear of you and of what you worship besides Allah. We reject you, and enmity and hatred have appeared between us and you forever, until you believe in Allah alone" (60:4). The same verse ends with their prayer: "Our Lord, in You we trust, to You we turn" (60:4). A Muslim learns that loyalty belongs first to Allah.

question: In Surah Ibrahim, what did Ibrahim ask for the city of Mecca?
answers: That it be secure, and that he and his sons be kept from worshipping idols
That it become a great market
explanation: "My Lord, make this city secure, and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols."
detail: The prayer opens: "My Lord, make this city secure, and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols. My Lord, they have led many of the people astray" (14:35-36). Ibrahim goes on to say that he has settled some of his offspring in a valley without cultivation near Allah's sacred House, and asks that hearts incline toward them and that they be provided with fruits (14:37). A Muslim learns from Ibrahim what to ask for one's children before food or comfort: that they worship Allah alone.

question: What did Ibrahim say as he left his people?
answers: "I am going to my Lord; He will guide me"
explanation: "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."
detail: Surah As-Saffat records: "He said: I am going to my Lord; He will guide me. My Lord, grant me one of the righteous. So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy" (37:99-101). The words come right after his people, beaten in argument over the idols he had broken, tried to burn him: "they plotted against him, but We made them the lowest" (37:98). A Muslim learns that leaving one's people for Allah's sake is a journey toward guidance, and its first fruit was a righteous son.

question: Of which prophet does the Quran say he was "true to his promise" and enjoined prayer and zakat on his family?
explanation: "He was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet. He used to enjoin on his family prayer and zakat."
detail: Surah Maryam says: "Mention in the Book Isma'il. He was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet. He used to command his family to prayer and zakat, and he was pleasing to his Lord" (19:54-55). He appears in the surah's series of prophets, after Musa and Harun (19:51-53) and before Idris (19:56). A Muslim learns that keeping one's word is a mark of prophethood, and that prayer and zakat begin at home.

question: What did Ya'qub advise Yusuf after his dream?
answers: Not to relate it to his brothers
explanation: "O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, or they will plot against you."
detail: Ya'qub says in Surah Yusuf: "O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, or they will plot against you. Satan is a clear enemy to man" (12:5). Yusuf had just told him: "O my father, I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me" (12:4). At the end of the surah Yusuf's family bows before him (12:100). A Muslim learns to guard a blessing from envy and trust Allah to bring it about.

question: What sign established Yusuf's innocence before the master of the house?
answers: His shirt torn from the back
explanation: If the shirt was torn from behind, she lied and he is among the truthful.
detail: Surah Yusuf records: "A witness from her family testified: if his shirt is torn from the front, she has told the truth and he is a liar; but if his shirt is torn from the back, she has lied and he is one of the truthful" (12:26-27). The next verse settles it: "When he saw his shirt torn from the back, he said: This is one of your women's schemes" (12:28). A Muslim learns that Allah brought Yusuf's innocence to light by a plain sign.

question: What did the women of the city do when they saw Yusuf?
answers: They cut their hands in astonishment
explanation: "When they saw him they exalted him and cut their hands, saying: 'This is no human being; this is but a noble angel.'"
detail: Surah Yusuf tells it: "She sent for them and prepared a banquet, gave each of them a knife, and said: Come out before them. When they saw him, they were struck with awe and cut their hands, and said: Allah forbid! This is no human; this is none but a noble angel" (12:31). She threatened him with prison, and Yusuf prayed: "My Lord, prison is dearer to me than what they call me to" (12:33). A Muslim learns that Yusuf chose prison over disobeying Allah.

question: What did Yusuf teach his two prison companions before interpreting their dreams?
answers: The oneness of Allah, and that judgement belongs to Him alone
explanation: "Are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Prevailing? … Judgement is only for Allah."
detail: Yusuf says: "O my two companions of the prison, are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Prevailing? You worship besides Him nothing but names that you and your fathers have invented, for which Allah has sent down no authority. Judgement belongs to Allah alone" (12:39-40). Two young men had asked him to interpret their dreams, seeing him as a doer of good (12:36). A Muslim learns to put the call to Allah's oneness before every other service.

question: What did the king of Egypt say to Yusuf after speaking with him?
answers: "Today you are established in position and trusted with us"
explanation: "And when he had spoken with him, he said: 'Indeed, you are today established in position and trusted.'"
detail: Surah Yusuf records: "The king said: Bring him to me; I will take him for myself. And when he had spoken with him, he said: Today you are, with us, established and trusted" (12:54). Yusuf had refused to leave prison until the matter of the women was cleared (12:50). He answered the king's offer with a request: "Set me over the storehouses of the land" (12:55). A Muslim learns that Yusuf's rank came after his honour was cleared, and he used it to take on a duty.

question: How did Yusuf keep his brother with him?
answers: The king's cup was found in his brother's bag
explanation: "Thus did We plan for Yusuf": the cup came out of his brother's bag.
detail: Surah Yusuf says: "He began with their bags before his brother's bag, then he brought it out of his brother's bag. Thus did We plan for Yusuf; he could not have taken his brother under the king's law unless Allah willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, and above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing" (12:76). The brothers themselves had named the penalty: the one in whose bag it was found would be kept (12:75). A Muslim learns that Allah arranges events beyond human sight.

question: What did Yusuf say to his brothers when they admitted their fault?
explanation: "No blame will there be upon you today. May Allah forgive you; He is the most merciful of the merciful."
detail: Yusuf's words are in Surah Yusuf: "No blame on you today. Allah will forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful" (12:92). He had asked whether they remembered what they did to Yusuf and his brother in their ignorance (12:89), then told them: "I am Yusuf, and this is my brother" (12:90); they admitted: "Allah has preferred you over us, and we were sinners" (12:91). A Muslim learns that forgiving those who wronged us, when we hold power over them, is the way of the prophets.

question: What did Ya'qub tell his sons about despair?
answers: "Do not despair of the mercy of Allah"
explanation: "Do not despair of relief from Allah: none despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people."
detail: Ya'qub says in Surah Yusuf: "O my sons, go and search for Yusuf and his brother, and do not despair of relief from Allah. None despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people" (12:87). By then his eyes had turned white from grief (12:84), and his sons had told him he would not stop remembering Yusuf until he wasted away (12:85). A Muslim learns that grief is brought to Allah, and that hope in His relief is part of faith itself.

question: What supplication did Yusuf make at the end of his story?
answers: To die in submission and be joined with the righteous
explanation: "Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous."
detail: The prayer reads: "My Lord, You have given me something of sovereignty and taught me the interpretation of events. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous" (12:101). Yusuf says it at the height of his story, when his parents have come to Egypt and his family has bowed before him (12:100). A Muslim learns from Yusuf to ask for a good ending above every worldly gain.

question: How did Ayyub address his Lord in his trial?
answers: "Adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful"
explanation: "And remember Our servant Ayyub, when he called to his Lord: 'Satan has touched me with hardship and torment.'"
detail: Surah Sad says: "Remember Our servant Ayyub, when he called to his Lord: Satan has touched me with hardship and suffering" (38:41). Surah Al-Anbiya gives his call in the words: "Adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful" (21:83). The answer came at once: "Strike with your foot; here is a cool spring for washing and drinking" (38:42). A Muslim learns from Ayyub how to complain to Allah alone, without a word against Him.

question: What did Allah restore to Ayyub after the trial, according to Surah Sad?
answers: His family, and the like of them with them
explanation: "And We granted him his family and a like number with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding."
detail: Surah Sad says: "We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for people of understanding" (38:43). The verse after adds Allah's testimony: "We found him patient. An excellent servant" (38:44). Surah Al-Anbiya says the same: "We answered him and removed the harm that was on him, and We gave him his family and the like of them with them" (21:84). A Muslim learns that Allah's relief after patience comes larger than the loss: what was lost was doubled.

question: According to Surah As-Saffat, what saved Yunus from remaining in the belly of the fish?
answers: That he was of those who glorify Allah
explanation: "And had he not been of those who exalt Allah, he would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected."
detail: Surah As-Saffat says: "Had he not been of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are raised" (37:143-144). Yunus had run away to the laden ship, drawn lots and lost (37:140-141). Surah Al-Anbiya gives his words in the darkness: "There is no god but You; glory be to You; I have been among the wrongdoers" (21:87). A Muslim learns that glorifying Allah in easy times carries a servant through the hardest ones.

question: Which people, according to the Quran, believed before the punishment reached them, and it benefited them?
explanation: "Then has there not been a city that believed and its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus?"
detail: Surah Yunus says: "If only there had been a city that believed and whose faith benefited it, other than the people of Yunus. When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and We let them enjoy for a time" (10:98). Surah As-Saffat gives their number: a hundred thousand or more, "and they believed" (37:147-148). A Muslim learns that repentance before the punishment arrives is accepted, and a whole city was spared by it.

question: How does the Quran name Yunus when the Prophet ﷺ is told not to be like him in impatience?
explanation: "And be not like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was distressed."
detail: Surah Al-Qalam says: "Be patient for the judgement of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was choked with grief. Had a favour from his Lord not reached him, he would have been cast on the bare shore, blamed. But his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous" (68:48-50). The surah is addressed to the Prophet ﷺ (68:2). A Muslim learns that patience is asked of the one who calls to Allah.

question: Which prophet rebuked his people for calling upon Ba'l and forsaking the best of creators?
explanation: "And indeed, Ilyas was among the messengers… 'Do you call upon Ba'l and leave the best of creators?'"
detail: Surah As-Saffat says: "Ilyas was one of the messengers, when he said to his people: Will you not fear Allah? Do you call upon Ba'l and forsake the best of creators, Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers?" (37:123-126). His people denied him (37:127); then Allah left him a greeting among later generations, "Peace be upon Ilyas" (37:129-130). A Muslim learns that Ilyas called to worship of the Creator alone, and that the peace sent on him is recited today.

question: Alongside Isma'il and Idris, which prophet does the Quran name among the patient whom Allah admitted into His mercy?
explanation: "And Isma'il, Idris and Dhul-Kifl — all were of the patient. And We admitted them into Our mercy."
detail: Surah Al-Anbiya says: "And Isma'il and Idris and Dhul-Kifl: all were of the patient. And We admitted them into Our mercy; they were among the righteous" (21:85-86). They are named right after Ayyub, whose patience in affliction has just been told (21:83-84). Dhul-Kifl is named once more in Surah Sad, again beside Isma'il: "Remember Isma'il and Al-Yasa' and Dhul-Kifl; all are among the best" (38:48). A Muslim learns that the Qur'an tells no story of him, and that patience alone earned him a place in Allah's mercy.

question: What did Allah do for the Children of Israel at the sea, pursued by Pharaoh?
answers: He parted the sea and saved them
explanation: "And when We parted the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh."
detail: Surah Al-Baqarah says: "When We parted the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were watching" (2:50). It belongs to a passage that begins "O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you" (2:40). Surah Ash-Shu'ara shows the moment: "Strike the sea with your staff. And it parted, and each part was like a great mountain" (26:63). A Muslim learns that Allah saves and judges in a single act, and that His favours are to be remembered.

question: Why did Musa ask Allah to send Harun with him?
answers: Because he was more eloquent in speech than he
explanation: "And my brother Harun is more fluent than me in speech, so send him with me as support, confirming me."
detail: Musa says in Surah Al-Qasas: "My brother Harun is more eloquent than me in speech, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me; I fear that they will deny me" (28:34). Allah answered: "We will strengthen your arm through your brother and give you both authority" (28:35). A Muslim learns that asking for a helper is no weakness, and that Allah granted Harun prophethood in answer to his brother's prayer.

question: How were Musa and Harun to speak to Pharaoh?
explanation: "And speak to him with gentle speech, that perhaps he may be reminded or fear Allah."
detail: Allah says to Musa and Harun in Surah Ta-Ha: "Speak to him with gentle words, so that he may take heed or fear" (20:44), right after "Go, both of you, to Pharaoh; he has transgressed" (20:43). The two answered: "Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us or transgress", and were told: "Do not fear; I am with you both, I hear and I see" (20:45-46). A Muslim learns that gentleness in calling to Allah is commanded even toward the hardest hearer.

question: Who from Pharaoh's household defended Musa while concealing his faith?
answers: A believing man of Pharaoh's family
explanation: "And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said: 'Do you kill a man because he says, my Lord is Allah?'"
detail: Surah Ghafir says: "A believing man from Pharaoh's family, who concealed his faith, said: Would you kill a man because he says: My Lord is Allah, when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?" (40:28). He speaks right after Pharaoh says "Let me kill Musa" (40:26), and the surah ends his story: "So Allah protected him from the evils they plotted" (40:45). A Muslim learns that one believer speaking truth before a tyrant is remembered by Allah.

question: What did Harun say to his people while Musa was away?
answers: That they were only being tested by the calf, and should follow him
explanation: "O my people, you are only being tested by it. Your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me."
detail: Surah Ta-Ha says: "Harun had told them before: O my people, you are only being tested by it. Your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command" (20:90). The Samiri had made them a calf, a body that lowed, and they said, "This is your god and the god of Musa" (20:88). A Muslim learns that a trial can come dressed as a wonder, and that following Allah's messenger, as Harun asked, is the way through it.

question: What did Pharaoh's wife say on finding the infant Musa?
answers: "He will be a comfort of the eye for me and for you: do not kill him"
explanation: "And the wife of Pharaoh said: 'A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us.'"
detail: Surah Al-Qasas says: "The wife of Pharaoh said: A comfort of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him. He may be of use to us, or we may take him as a son. And they did not perceive" (28:9). Musa's mother had been inspired to cast him into the river (28:7). In Surah At-Tahrim the same woman prays: "My Lord, build for me a house near You in Paradise" (66:11). A Muslim learns that a believing heart lived inside Pharaoh's own palace.

question: How did Musa ask to follow the knowledgeable servant (al-Khidr)?
answers: "May I follow you, on condition that you teach me?"
explanation: "May I follow you on condition that you teach me from what you have been taught of right guidance?"
detail: Surah Al-Kahf records: "Musa said to him: May I follow you, on condition that you teach me some of the right guidance you have been taught?" (18:66). The man is described only as "a servant from among Our servants, to whom We had given mercy from Us and taught knowledge from Us" (18:65). Musa promised: "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient" (18:69). A Muslim learns the manners of seeking knowledge from Musa, the prophet who spoke with Allah: ask permission, promise patience, and put oneself under the teacher.

question: In what state did Musa return to his people after seeing the calf?
explanation: "And when Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved… he threw down the tablets."
detail: Surah Al-A'raf says: "When Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said: How evil is what you did in my place after me! He threw down the tablets and seized his brother by the head" (7:150). Harun answered: "Son of my mother, the people overpowered me and nearly killed me" (7:150), and Musa prayed: "My Lord, forgive me and my brother" (7:151). A Muslim learns that anger for Allah's sake is real even in a prophet, and that it ends in prayer.

question: What message was Musa to bring Pharaoh according to Surah An-Nazi'at?
answers: "Would you purify yourself, and let me guide you to your Lord?"
explanation: "Go to Pharaoh; he has transgressed. And say: would you purify yourself, and let me guide you to your Lord so you would fear Him?"
detail: Surah An-Nazi'at says: "Go to Pharaoh; he has transgressed. And say: Would you be willing to purify yourself, and that I guide you to your Lord, so that you may fear Him?" (79:17-19). The surah has just recalled Musa's call in the sacred valley of Tuwa (79:15-16). Pharaoh answered by proclaiming "I am your most exalted lord" (79:24), so Allah seized him as an example (79:25). A Muslim learns that even a tyrant was first offered purification and guidance, with a question rather than a threat.

question: Who glorified Allah together with Dawud, evening and morning?
explanation: "We subjected the mountains to glorify with him in the evening and after sunrise, and the birds, gathered together."
detail: Surah Sad tells the Prophet ﷺ to remember Dawud, "possessor of strength", who constantly turned back to his Lord (38:17), then describes his companions in praise: "Indeed, We subjected the mountains to exalt with him in the evening and after sunrise, and the birds, assembled, all turning to Him with him" (38:18-19). Mountains and birds joined a prophet in remembering Allah at both ends of the day. A Muslim takes from this that glorifying Allah morning and evening joins a person to the praise of all creation.

question: What does the Quran say Allah gave Dawud, along with a firm kingdom?
explanation: "And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and discernment in speech."
detail: The verse follows the mountains and birds that glorified with Dawud: "And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive speech" (38:20). The next verses show that speech in use, when two disputants climbed over the wall of his prayer chamber and asked him to judge between them justly (38:21-22). A firm kingdom, wisdom and clear words to settle a matter are named together as gifts from Allah, not achievements of a king. A Muslim learns that authority is only sound when joined to wisdom and just judgement.

question: What was Dawud commanded regarding the coats of mail he made?
answers: To engrave his name on them
explanation: "Make full coats of mail, and measure precisely the links."
detail: Surah Saba first lists what Allah gave Dawud: the mountains and birds repeating praise with him, and iron made soft for him (34:10). The command then follows: "Make full coats of mail and measure precisely the links, and work righteousness; indeed I am Seeing of what you do" (34:11). The verse pairs careful craftsmanship with righteous conduct, and closes by reminding Dawud that Allah watches the work. A Muslim takes from it that doing a task well, down to its smallest measure, is itself part of worship.

question: What did Dawud and Sulaiman say when Allah gave them knowledge?
answers: "Praise to Allah, who has favoured us over many of His believing servants"
explanation: "Praise be to Allah, who has favoured us over many of His believing servants."
detail: The verse opens the story of Sulaiman: "And We had given to Dawud and Sulaiman knowledge, and they said: Praise be to Allah, who has favoured us over many of His believing servants" (27:15). The next verse tells that Sulaiman inherited Dawud and announced that he had been taught the speech of birds and given from all things (27:16). Father and son received knowledge and answered it with praise. A Muslim learns to meet every gift of understanding with thanks to the One who gave it.

question: What did Sulaiman do on hearing the ant warn her people?
answers: He smiled and asked Allah to make him grateful
He turned his army aside in silence
explanation: "So he smiled, amused at her speech, and said: 'My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour.'"
detail: In the valley of the ants, an ant cried: "O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Sulaiman and his soldiers crush you while they perceive not" (27:18). "So he smiled, amused at her speech, and said: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness of which You approve" (27:19). A king turned a tiny creature's warning into a prayer of thanks. A Muslim learns to answer every reminder of Allah's favour with gratitude.

question: What news did the hoopoe bring Sulaiman?
answers: A woman ruled Saba and her people prostrated to the sun
explanation: "I have come to you from Saba with certain news: I found a woman ruling them… they prostrate to the sun."
detail: Sulaiman had noticed the hoopoe missing and promised it a severe punishment unless it brought a clear reason (27:20-21). The bird returned and said: "I have come to you from Saba with certain news. I found a woman ruling them, and she has a great throne" (27:22-23). It said that she and her people prostrated to the sun (27:24). Sulaiman replied that he would test whether the report was true (27:27). A Muslim learns that news is worth acting on only once it has been verified.

question: What astonished the queen of Saba on entering Sulaiman's palace?
answers: The floor of glass, which she took for water
explanation: "She was told: 'Enter the palace.' Seeing it, she thought it a body of water and bared her shins. He said: 'It is a palace paved with glass.'"
detail: Her own throne had already been brought before her (27:42). Then "she was told: Enter the palace. But when she saw it, she thought it was a body of water and uncovered her shins. He said: It is a palace made smooth with glass" (27:44). In that same verse she answered: "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Sulaiman to Allah, Lord of the worlds." A Muslim takes from this that recognising one's error and turning to Allah matters more than any wonder.

question: What were Sulaiman's armies made up of, according to the Quran?
explanation: "And gathered for Sulaiman were his soldiers of the jinn and men and birds, and they were set in rows."
detail: "And gathered for Sulaiman were his soldiers of the jinn and men and birds, and they were set in rows" (27:17). This follows his words that he had been taught the speech of birds and given from all things (27:16), and it leads straight into the valley of the ants (27:18). Three kinds of creatures marched under one prophet-king, in order, because Allah had placed them under his command. A Muslim learns that Sulaiman's power came from Allah, who presents it as a favour calling for thanks (27:19).

question: How did Zakariyya describe his state when calling on his Lord?
answers: "My bones have weakened and my head has filled with white"
explanation: "My Lord, my bones have weakened and my head has filled with white, and never have I been unblessed in my supplication to You."
detail: Surah Maryam opens with the mercy shown to Zakariyya when he called on his Lord privately (19:3). He said: "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled with white, and never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unblessed" (19:4). He then asked for an heir, since his wife was barren (19:5-6), and was given good tidings of a boy named Yahya (19:7). A Muslim learns to bring weakness and old age before Allah in quiet, trusting prayer.

question: What sign was given to Zakariyya for the birth of Yahya?
answers: Not to speak to people for three days except by gesture
explanation: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture."
detail: Zakariyya had prayed for good offspring (3:38), and the angels brought him good tidings of Yahya (3:39). When he asked how he could have a son in old age, he was told: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture" (3:41), and to remember his Lord much and glorify Him evening and morning. The sign was silence toward people, joined to remembrance of Allah. A Muslim takes from it that a gift from Allah is met with more remembrance, not less.

question: What was Yahya told concerning the Scripture?
explanation: "O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination." And We gave him judgement while yet a boy.
detail: The address to Yahya follows the story of his birth: "O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination. And We gave him judgement while yet a boy" (19:12). The verses that follow describe him: tenderness from Allah and purity, fear of Allah, and dutifulness to his parents (19:13-14). Then comes a greeting: "And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he is raised alive" (19:15). A Muslim learns that holding firmly to Allah's Book is expected even of the young.

question: What did the angels command Maryam after announcing that she was chosen?
answers: To be devoutly obedient to her Lord, to prostrate and to bow
To set out on a journey
explanation: "O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow."
detail: Just before this, the angels said: "O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds" (3:42). Then came the command: "O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow" (3:43). Earlier, Allah had accepted her, caused her to grow well and placed her in the care of Zakariyya (3:37). Being chosen was answered with more worship, not pride. A Muslim learns that honour from Allah is carried by humility and prayer.

question: What was Maryam told to shake for food at the time of the birth?
answers: The trunk of the palm tree, to drop fresh dates
explanation: "And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates."
detail: Childbirth drove Maryam to a palm trunk, where she wished she had died (19:23). Then a voice called from below her: "Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream. And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates. So eat and drink and be contented" (19:24-26). Provision was given, yet she was still told to shake the trunk herself. A Muslim learns that Allah's provision is near, and that a person still makes the effort asked of them.

question: What did 'Isa say in the cradle that Allah had enjoined on him?
answers: Prayer and zakat, as long as he lived
explanation: "And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I remain alive."
detail: When Maryam pointed to the child, her people asked how they could speak to one in the cradle (19:29). He answered that he was Allah's servant, given the Scripture and made a prophet (19:30), then: "And He has made me blessed wherever I am, and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I remain alive" (19:31), and dutiful to his mother (19:32). A Muslim learns that prayer and zakat bind a person for life, as they bound 'Isa.

question: How does Surah Az-Zukhruf describe 'Isa son of Maryam?
answers: A servant upon whom Allah bestowed favour and made an example for the Children of Israel
explanation: "He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel."
detail: The verse answers people who laughed when 'Isa was mentioned as an example and asked whether their gods were better than he (43:57-58). "He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel" (43:59). Later in the surah 'Isa himself says: "Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path" (43:64). A Muslim honours 'Isa as a prophet and servant, and worships only the Lord he worshipped.

question: What will 'Isa answer on the Day of Resurrection when Allah questions him?
answers: "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say what I had no right to say"
explanation: "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right."
detail: Allah will ask 'Isa on the Day of Resurrection whether he told people to take him and his mother as gods besides Allah (5:116). He will answer: "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it" (5:116). He will add that he told them only what he was commanded: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord" (5:117). A Muslim learns from 'Isa's own words that he called to Allah alone.

question: How does the Quran describe 'Isa son of Maryam?
answers: The messenger of Allah, His word conveyed to Maryam, and a spirit from Him
explanation: "The Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Maryam and a soul from Him."
detail: The verse addresses the People of the Scripture against excess in religion (4:171). It then states who 'Isa is: "The Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Maryam and a soul from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say Three" (4:171). The next verse adds that the Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of Allah (4:172). A Muslim speaks of 'Isa as the Qur'an does: messenger, word and spirit from Allah.

question: In Surah Ad-Duha, which favours does Allah remind His Prophet ﷺ of?
answers: He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him and enriched him
explanation: "Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge? And find you lost and guide you? And find you poor and make you self-sufficient?"
detail: Surah Ad-Duha first assures the Prophet ﷺ that his Lord has not left him (93:3). Then come the three favours: "Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge? And He found you lost and guided you. And He found you poor and made you self-sufficient" (93:6-8). The surah closes by turning the favours into duties: do not oppress the orphan, do not repel the one who asks, and speak of your Lord's favour (93:9-11). A Muslim learns to remember past blessings and give as he was given.

question: Which promise does Surah Ash-Sharh repeat twice?
explanation: "For indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease."
detail: Surah Ash-Sharh first recalls three gifts to the Prophet ﷺ: the opening of his breast, the lifting of his burden and the raising of his name (94:1-4). Then comes the promise, twice: "For indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease" (94:5-6). Then: "So when you have finished, then stand up, and to your Lord direct your longing" (94:7-8). The words say "with" hardship, not "after" it: ease is already beside the difficulty. A Muslim learns to hold on in hard times.

question: What was the Prophet ﷺ granted in Surah Al-Kawthar, and what was he ordered in return?
answers: Al-Kawthar; to pray to his Lord and sacrifice
explanation: "Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice."
detail: The surah has three verses: "Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off" (108:1-3). It begins with a gift given, moves to the two acts asked in return, prayer and sacrifice, and ends by turning the insult of the enemy back on him. The name al-Kawthar comes from a root meaning abundance. A Muslim learns that the right answer to a gift from Allah is worship directed to Him alone.

question: How does Surah At-Tawbah describe the Messenger ﷺ toward the believers?
answers: Concerned for them, kind and merciful
explanation: "There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves… concerned over you, and to the believers kind and merciful."
detail: Surah At-Tawbah ends with these verses: "There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you, and to the believers is kind and merciful" (9:128). If they turn away, he is to say: "Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied" (9:129). The Messenger ﷺ is described as one of the people, and resting on Allah alone. A Muslim learns to care for others as the Prophet ﷺ cared.

question: According to the Quran, what would have driven people away from the Prophet ﷺ, had he been so?
answers: Had he been rude and harsh of heart
explanation: "So by mercy from Allah you were lenient with them. Had you been rude and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you."
detail: The verse belongs to the passage that reviews the battle of Uhud (3:152-155). "So by mercy from Allah you were lenient with them. And if you had been rude and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter" (3:159). His gentleness is named a mercy from Allah, and it is followed by pardon, prayer and consultation. A Muslim learns that softness of heart holds people together where harshness scatters them.

question: What does the Quran say of Allah's Messenger ﷺ for those who hope in Allah and the Last Day?
answers: He is for them an excellent example
explanation: "There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern, for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day."
detail: The verse stands in the account of the Confederates, when armies came and "eyes shifted and hearts reached the throats" (33:10). "There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day" (33:21). The next verse shows the believers saying this was what Allah and His Messenger had promised, which only increased their faith (33:22). A Muslim learns to look to the Prophet ﷺ for how to act in every situation.

question: To whom was the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ sent, according to Surah Saba?
explanation: "And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner to all mankind."
detail: "And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind, as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, but most of the people do not know" (34:28). The verse follows the story of Saba (34:15-19). Elsewhere the Prophet ﷺ is told to say: "O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all" (7:158), and he is called "a mercy to the worlds" (21:107). His message is not for one tribe or one land. A Muslim learns that the call of Muhammad ﷺ reaches every person.

question: Which verse did the Prophet ﷺ recite as the idols around the Ka'bah were removed?
answers: "Truth has come and falsehood has departed"
"We have given you a clear victory"
explanation: "And say: Truth has come and falsehood has departed. Indeed, falsehood is bound to depart."
detail: "And say: Truth has come and falsehood has departed. Indeed, falsehood is bound to depart" (17:81). Before it, the Prophet ﷺ is taught to pray for a sound entrance, a sound exit and a supporting authority from Allah (17:80), and right after it the Qur'an is called "healing and mercy for the believers" (17:82). The sira records him reciting the verse at the conquest of Makkah as the idols around the Ka'bah fell. A Muslim repeats the verse knowing that whatever stands against the truth has no lasting hold.

question: What do the believers say about Allah's messengers, at the end of Surah Al-Baqarah?
answers: "We make no distinction between any of His messengers"
explanation: "We make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they said: we hear and we obey."
detail: The second-last verse of Surah Al-Baqarah describes the faith of the Messenger ﷺ and the believers: "All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, saying: We make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they say: We hear and we obey" (2:285). The verse that follows is the prayer "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or err" (2:286). A Muslim believes in all the prophets, without leaving one out, and joins that belief to obedience.

question: What single message did every messenger bring his people?
answers: "Worship Allah and avoid false objects of worship"
explanation: "And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, saying: worship Allah and avoid taghut."
detail: "And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, saying: Worship Allah and avoid taghut. And among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was decreed. So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers" (16:36). No nation was left without a messenger, and every messenger opened with the same call. The verse then points to the ruins of those who refused. A Muslim learns that the religion of all the prophets is one: worship Allah alone.

question: In what language was each messenger sent, according to Surah Ibrahim?
answers: In the tongue of his own people, to make things clear
explanation: "And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people, to state clearly for them."
detail: "And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people, to make things clear for them" (14:4). The surah has just described the Book sent down "that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light" (14:1), and the next verse recalls Musa sent with the same charge to his people (14:5). A message meant to be understood is delivered in words the hearers already know. A Muslim learns that Allah's guidance is meant to be understood, not merely heard.

question: What was revealed to every messenger before Muhammad ﷺ, according to Surah Al-Anbiya?
answers: That there is no deity except Him, so worship Him
explanation: "And We sent not before you any messenger except that We revealed to him: there is no deity except Me, so worship Me."
detail: "And We sent not before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me" (21:25). Before it, those who take gods besides Allah are told, "Produce your proof" (21:24), and after it the claim that the Most Merciful has taken a son is rejected: "Rather, they are honoured servants" (21:26). Every revelation before the Qur'an carried the same first sentence. A Muslim learns that "there is no god but Allah" is the oldest message of all.

question: In Surah Al-An'am, which group of prophets is listed as the guided offspring of Ibrahim?
answers: Dawud, Sulaiman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa and Harun among others
explanation: The passage lists a long line of prophets whom Allah guided, saying: "And thus do We reward the doers of good."
detail: Ibrahim's line is named: "And We gave to him Ishaq and Ya'qub; all of them We guided. And Nuh We guided before, and among his descendants Dawud and Sulaiman and Ayyub and Yusuf and Musa and Harun" (6:84). The list continues with Zakariyya, Yahya, 'Isa and Ilyas, then Isma'il, Alyasa', Yunus and Lut (6:85-86): seventeen prophets in three verses. The passage then says: "Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, so from their guidance take an example" (6:90). A Muslim learns their names as one family of guidance.

question: What does the Quran say about the messengers in relation to one another?
answers: Allah favoured some of them above others
They are all identical in rank
They knew nothing of each other
explanation: "Those messengers — some of them We caused to exceed others."
detail: "Those messengers, some of them We caused to exceed others. Among them were those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in degree. And We gave 'Isa, son of Maryam, clear proofs and supported him with the Pure Spirit" (2:253). The verse sits beside the believers' words in the same surah, "We make no distinction between any of His messengers" (2:285). Allah ranks His messengers, while the believer honours every one of them. A Muslim believes in all the messengers and leaves their ranking to Allah.

question: What covenant did Allah take from the prophets, according to Surah Al-'Imran?
answers: To believe in the Messenger who would come confirming what they had, and to support him
explanation: "If a Messenger comes to you confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him."
detail: "And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: Whatever I give you of the Scripture and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him" (3:81). They acknowledged the pledge, and Allah made them witnesses to it (3:81). The next verse adds that whoever turns away after this is defiantly disobedient (3:82). The prophets themselves pledged to accept the messenger confirming their books. A Muslim learns that following Muhammad ﷺ fulfils what every earlier prophet promised.

question: Which prophets does the Quran name in saying Allah ordained for them the same religion?
answers: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and 'Isa, along with what was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ
explanation: "He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Nuh, and what We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Ibrahim, Musa and 'Isa."
detail: "He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Nuh, and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Ibrahim and Musa and 'Isa: establish the religion and do not be divided therein" (42:13). Five names stand in the verse: four earlier prophets and the Prophet ﷺ, addressed as "you". What was given to all of them is described as one religion, with one instruction: do not split over it. A Muslim learns that Islam is the religion of Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and 'Isa.

question: What does the Quran say about messengers whose stories it does not tell?
answers: There are some whose story Allah did not relate to the Prophet ﷺ
explanation: "Among them are those whose story We have related to you, and among them are those whose story We have not related to you."
detail: "And We have already sent messengers before you. Among them are those whose story We have related to you, and among them are those whose story We have not related to you" (40:78). The same statement appears in Surah An-Nisa, where after listing messengers Allah adds "and messengers about whom We have not related to you" (4:164). The Qur'an names some prophets and is silent about the rest. A Muslim believes in every messenger Allah sent, named or unnamed, without inventing stories for the rest.

question: From whom did Allah choose all His messengers, according to Surah Yusuf?
answers: Men of the towns, to whom He sent revelation
explanation: "And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed, from among the people of the cities."
detail: "And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed, from among the people of the cities" (12:109). The verse comes at the close of Surah Yusuf, after Yusuf's long story, and just before the surah says that in the stories of the messengers "there was a lesson for those of understanding" (12:111). Messengers were men, living in towns, speaking to their neighbours. A Muslim learns that the prophets were human beings whose lives can be followed.

question: What does the Quran recall about messengers denied before Muhammad ﷺ?
answers: They were patient until Our help came to them
explanation: "Certainly were messengers denied before you, but they were patient over the denial until Our victory came to them."
detail: "And certainly were messengers denied before you, but they were patient over the denial and were harmed until Our victory came to them. And none can alter the words of Allah" (6:34). The verse before it speaks to the Prophet ﷺ directly: "We know that you are saddened by what they say" (6:33). The comfort offered is the record of the earlier messengers: denial, patience, harm, then help. A Muslim learns that patience under rejection is the way of every prophet, and that Allah's help follows it.

question: Which families did Allah choose above the worlds, according to Surah Al-'Imran?
answers: Adam, Nuh, the family of Ibrahim and the family of 'Imran
explanation: "Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Nuh and the family of Ibrahim and the family of 'Imran above the worlds."
detail: "Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Nuh and the family of Ibrahim and the family of 'Imran over the worlds, descendants, some of them from others" (3:33-34). The verse opens the passage that tells how the wife of 'Imran vowed the child in her womb to Allah's service and gave birth to Maryam (3:35-36). The chosen families are linked as one line of descent. A Muslim learns that the prophets belong to a single chain of chosen people, and honours the family of Maryam within it.

question: Which favours did Musa recall to his people, inviting them to enter the Holy Land?
answers: That Allah made prophets among them and made them kings
explanation: "O my people, remember the favour of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you kings."
detail: "And when Musa said to his people: O my people, remember the favour of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you kings. O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you, and do not turn back and become losers" (5:20-21). The people answered that a mighty folk lived there, and said: "Go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are remaining right here" (5:22-24). A Muslim learns that remembering Allah's favours is meant to give courage to obey Him.

question: How did the Torah and the Gospel describe the unlettered Prophet, according to the Quran?
answers: He enjoins right, forbids wrong and relieves them of their burdens
explanation: "…the unlettered prophet whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids what is wrong… and relieves them of their burden."
detail: The verse describes those who follow "the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and relieves them of their burden" (7:157). It comes as Allah answers Musa's prayer, promising mercy to those who follow this prophet (7:156). Those who believe in him and follow his light are called the successful (7:157). A Muslim learns that the earlier scriptures pointed ahead to Muhammad ﷺ.

question: On whom did Nuh say he relied, challenging his people to plot?
answers: On Allah, in whom he placed his trust
explanation: "Upon Allah do I rely. So resolve upon your plan, you and your associates."
detail: Nuh said to his people: "O my people, if my residence and my reminding of the signs of Allah has become burdensome upon you, then upon Allah I have relied. So resolve upon your plan, you and your associates, and give me no respite" (10:71). He asked no payment; his reward was from Allah alone (10:72). They denied him, and Allah saved him and those with him in the ship (10:73). A Muslim learns that whoever relies on Allah can face any plot without fear.

question: In Ibrahim's supplication, to whom does he attribute healing when he is ill?
explanation: "And when I am ill, it is He who cures me," said Ibrahim, describing his Lord.
detail: Ibrahim said this after asking his father and his people what they worshipped, and calling their idols his enemies (26:70-77). He then described his Lord: "Who created me, and He guides me; and it is He who feeds me and gives me drink; and when I am ill, it is He who cures me; and who will cause me to die and then bring me to life" (26:78-81). He ends by hoping for forgiveness on the Day of Recompense (26:82). A Muslim learns to seek healing from Allah first.

question: With what was Ibrahim's son ransomed, according to Surah As-Saffat?
explanation: "And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice."
detail: Ibrahim had been given a forbearing boy in answer to prayer (37:100-101). Grown, the boy heard the dream and answered: "O my father, do as you are commanded; you will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast" (37:102). When both had submitted and Ibrahim laid him down on his forehead, Allah called: "O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision" (37:103-105), and then: "And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice" (37:107). A Muslim learns that when father and son surrendered, Allah provided the way out.

question: What do the believers declare belief in, in the verse "Say: we have believed in Allah…"?
answers: In what was revealed to Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, Musa, 'Isa and the prophets
explanation: "Say: we have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub…"
detail: "Say: We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to Ibrahim and Isma'il and Ishaq and Ya'qub and the Descendants, and what was given to Musa and 'Isa, and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them" (2:136). The verse answers those who said "Be Jews or Christians" with "Rather, the religion of Ibrahim" (2:135). A Muslim's faith is spelled out here as one declaration covering every prophet.

question: Why does Allah relate the stories of the messengers to the Prophet ﷺ?
explanation: "And each story We relate to you from the news of the messengers is that by which We make firm your heart."
detail: "And each story We relate to you from the news of the messengers is that by which We make firm your heart. And there has come to you in this the truth and an instruction and a reminder for the believers" (11:120). The verse comes near the end of Surah Hud, which has told of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut, Shu'ayb and Musa. The stories have a stated purpose: to steady the Prophet ﷺ. A Muslim reads the lives of the prophets as strength for the heart in hard times.

question: What was the Prophet ﷺ told to say of himself at the end of Surah Al-Kahf?
answers: "I am only a man like you; it has been revealed that your God is one God"
explanation: "Say: I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your God is one God."
detail: This is the last verse of Surah Al-Kahf: "Say: I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your God is one God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone" (18:110). After the surah's long stories, the closing word is the Prophet's ﷺ humanity and Allah's oneness. A Muslim learns that a prophet is a man who receives revelation, and that pure worship is what Allah asks.

question: How does Surah Al-Fath describe those who are with the Messenger ﷺ?
answers: Firm against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves
explanation: "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves."
detail: Surah Al-Fath ends: "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration" (48:29). The same verse says this is their description in the Torah, and gives their likeness in the Gospel as a crop growing firm on its stalk. Firmness and mercy are joined, and both flow from bowing to Allah. A Muslim learns that the companions' strength grew from their worship.

question: What does Surah An-Najm say of the Prophet's ﷺ speech?
answers: He does not speak from desire: it is only a revelation revealed
He speaks of his own accord
explanation: "Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred, nor does he speak from his own inclination. It is not but a revelation revealed."
detail: Surah An-Najm opens with an oath by the star, then says: "Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred, nor does he speak from his own inclination. It is not but a revelation revealed, taught to him by one intense in strength" (53:2-5). The Prophet ﷺ is called "your companion", the man his people had known, and what he speaks is declared to be revelation, not his own wish. A Muslim receives the Prophet's ﷺ words as revelation, because the Qur'an itself says they are.

question: What was the Prophet ﷺ commanded when the help of Allah and the victory came?
answers: To glorify his Lord with praise and seek His forgiveness
explanation: "When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest… then exalt your Lord with praise and ask His forgiveness."
detail: The surah has three verses: "When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest, and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes, then exalt with praise of your Lord and ask forgiveness of Him. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance" (110:1-3). It is a whole surah about how to receive success: not with celebration of oneself, but with glorifying Allah and seeking His pardon. A Muslim learns to answer every victory with praise and istighfar.

question: Which three tasks does Surah Al-Jumu'ah give the Messenger sent to the unlettered?
answers: To recite the verses, purify them, and teach them the Book and wisdom
explanation: "It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom."
detail: "It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom" (62:2). The same tasks appear in the prayer Ibrahim made: "Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them" (2:129). The prayer and the sending describe one man. A Muslim learns that Muhammad ﷺ is the answer to Ibrahim's prayer.

question: What safeguard does the Quran mention while the Prophet ﷺ was among them?
answers: Allah would not punish them while he was among them
explanation: "But Allah would not punish them while you are among them."
detail: "But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness" (8:33).
